criteria_scores.criterion: Caching logic is encapsulated in a dedicated service module implementing a cache-aside pattern with defined TTL constants and explicit key invalidation on write endpoints.
criteria_scores.note: Caching logic is encapsulated in `cache.js` with defined `TTL_SECONDS` constants and `getOrSet()` loader logic, and `routes.js` explicitly invokes `cache.invalidateProduct()` on POST and PUT write endpoints.

criteria_scores.criterion: Web security hardening is visible through configured security headers middleware (e.g., Helmet), strict CORS origin settings, input validation schemas on POST/PUT endpoints, and parameterized database queries.
criteria_scores.note: Web security features are implemented in `app.js` using Helmet and a strict CORS origin allow-list, enforced via strict Zod schemas in `schemas.js` on write routes, and secured with prepared SQLite statements in `db.js`.

criteria_scores.criterion: The test suite contains separate test files for unit tests (verifying cache key generation and validation logic) and integration tests (verifying API response codes, security headers, and cache-hit/miss behavior).
criteria_scores.note: The test directory separates unit tests (`tests/unit/cache.test.js` and `tests/unit/schemas.test.js`) from integration tests (`tests/integration/api.test.js` and `tests/integration/security.test.js`) covering HTTP status codes, security headers, and cache HIT/MISS states.

feedback: You built an extraordinarily clean, modular, and thorough full-stack application with a well-designed cache-aside layer, strong security controls, and high-quality automated tests. To take this architecture to the next level, consider replacing the in-memory Map in `cache.js` with an external Redis client so the cache layer can be shared across multiple server instances without drifting out of sync.
